title: Crash landing for K-dramas? Waning output threatens genre’s future - South China Morning Post

Crash landing for K-dramas? Waning output threatens genre’s future | South China Morning Post East Asia - East Asia Crash landing for K-dramas? Waning output threatens genre’s future Advertisement South Korea Asia East Asia Crash landing for K-dramas? Waning output threatens genre’s future 
 South Korean ⁠industry groups seek government’s support and investment to prevent the sector’s collapse
 1 -MIN READ 1 -MIN Listen Reuters Published: 1:14pm, 4 Nov 2026 Twelve South Korean ⁠industry groups ⁠urged the government ⁠on Wednesday to invest in and support production of Korean television dramas, known as K-dramas , warning that the country’s production ‌base risked collapse. K-dramas have been hugely popular globally, but the number produced has fallen about 30 per cent from 141 titles in 2022, according to the Korea Drama Production Association.
 Three domestic ⁠broadcast networks cut drama output from 91 titles in ‌2012 to 32 in 2023, and some channels had stopped airing weekday ‌dramas altogether, the groups, which represent industry workers ⁠including ⁠television drama producers, directors, writers, actors, cinematographers and crew, said.
